subject: Nanotechnology
title: Template-Assisted Growth
description: A micro-lesson that makes Template-Assisted Growth usable.

hook.text: Fill the pores of a membrane with metal and dissolve the membrane — perfect nanowires remain standing.

buildup.text: Anodized alumina membranes have parallel pores just 20 to 200 nm wide — ideal molds for nanowires.

discovery.text: Electrodeposit gold, nickel, or polymers into the pores, then etch the alumina away to free the wires.

twist.text: Multi-segment nanowires are possible — deposit gold, then nickel, then gold — creating striped nano-barcodes.

climax.text: Nano-barcodes are used as multiplexed biosensors — each stripe pattern encodes a different analyte tag.

punchline.text: A membrane mold turns simple plating into precision nanowires.

quiz.question: How are striped nano-barcodes fabricated?
options: By painting alternating layers on a flat surface
By sequentially electrodepositing different metals into template pores
By dipping nanowires into colored dye solutions
